newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle lower, specs late sellers.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle lower, specs late sellers.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended weaker amid a late-session bout of speculative selling, traders said.

While the market has remained oversold technically, further losses may be in store in the near term, analysts said. Nearby support basis May was pegged at the recent low of 72.10 cents hit on April 9, and then at 65.50 cents, a low made in 1993, PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko, said.
Market sources agree that fundamental factors continue to drive the market. In particular, burgeoning supplies amid weak demand and high retail prices should keep pressure on prices.
"The market keeps looking like it wants to rally but fails because of the perception of oversupplies," Savaiko said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release the next Florida crop estimate on May 12. The last report pegged the crop at a record 221.2 million 90-lb boxes, and yields at 1.57 gallons per box.
Brazil will release its crop estimate on May 20 amid expectations for record production.
Most-active July closed 1.20 cents lower at 77.30 cents per lb, having traded from 79.50 to 77.20. May finished down 0.95 at 74.55 cents.
Estimated turnover was 4,500 lots compared with Friday's official 1,388 lots.
